evals.prompt:
Write BDD feature files for this acceptance criterion:
**Story:** As an API user, I want to retrieve an order by ID, so that I can display its details.
**AC-1:** Given a valid order ID, when the client requests GET /orders/{id}, then the response is 200 with the order payload.
**AC-2:** Given an order ID that does not exist, when the client requests GET /orders/{id}, then the response is 404 with an error message.
**AC-3:** Given an unauthenticated request, when the client requests GET /orders/{id}, then the response is 401.
evals.expected_output: A feature file at tests/features/order_retrieval.feature with: Feature declaration, and at least 3 scenarios (one per AC). Each scenario uses Given/When/Then with domain language (not implementation details). Plus a step stub file at tests/features/steps/test_order_retrieval.py with pytest-bdd @given/@when/@then decorators and pass stubs. Output must NOT reference internal function names.

assertions.text: Feature file placed at tests/features/ (not output/bdd/)
Three scenarios covering AC-1 (200), AC-2 (404), AC-3 (401)
No implementation code in the step stubs (only pass or TODOs)

evals.prompt: You are asked to write BDD scenarios for a hardware NFC reader module. The request comes from the bdd-writer-greenfield skill.
evals.expected_output: The skill should recognize this is an archaeology/hardware domain and redirect: 'This request involves hardware/legacy domain analysis. Use bdd-writer (the archaeology variant) instead. bdd-writer-greenfield is for new feature development driven by acceptance criteria.'

assertions.text: Skill correctly identifies this is out of scope for bdd-writer-greenfield
Skill redirects to bdd-writer (archaeology variant) rather than attempting to write hardware scenarios
